question: What two main elements make up the foundation of modern professional nursing?
explanation: Nursing combines the emotional and human connection of art with the empirical clinical knowledge of science to care for patients effectively. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is relying only on medical facts without empathy not enough for a nurse?

options.A: It automatically leads to immediate legal prosecution
options.B: It prevents the nurse from writing doctors' prescriptions
options.C: It misses the human touch needed for true healing
options.D: It violates standard hospital financial guidelines

explanation: You've got this! Clinical facts alone cannot address the emotional and spiritual suffering of a sick human being. Great nursing always requires genuine compassion. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: Who is widely recognized as the pioneer of modern professional nursing?
explanation: Florence Nightingale transformed nursing during the Crimean War by emphasizing sanitation, organization, and formal training. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: How has the primary role of the nurse changed from early historical times to today?

options.A: It evolved from informal domestic charity to an autonomous regulated profession
options.B: It changed from independent medical diagnosis to unpaid domestic work
options.C: It shifted from hospital administration to strictly religious duties
options.D: It transformed from a male-only military role to a purely clerical office job

explanation: Think about how far we've come! Modern nursing requires formal education, licensing, and independent critical thinking, rather than just basic home caregiving. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which global body defines nursing as autonomous and collaborative care for people of all ages in all settings?
explanation: Spot on! The International Council of Nurses sets the global standard definition that highlights both our independent and teamwork roles in healthcare. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of these activities is a core part of the global definition of nursing?

options.A: Filing hospital tax returns and insurance claims
options.B: Promoting healthy lifestyles in local communities
options.C: Purchasing pharmaceutical drugs for wholesale markets
options.D: Designing architectural layouts for new surgical suites

explanation: Nursing goes beyond treating sick people in wards; we also actively promote health and prevent illness right inside our communities! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four central concepts in the nursing metaparadigm?
explanation: Easy to remember: the four pillars are Person, Environment, Health, and Nursing. Medication is just a tool we use, not a core pillar! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: How do nursing theorists define 'health' within our professional framework?

options.A: A dynamic state of physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: The complete elimination of all hospital admissions nationwide
options.C: The total absence of any identifiable bacteria in the blood
options.D: A static condition achieved strictly through pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Health isn't just the literal absence of sickness. In nursing, we see it as a flowing, everyday state of overall physical, mental, and social well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: When a nurse steps up to protect a patient's rights and safety, what role are they playing?
explanation: You got it! Being an advocate means standing up for your patients' rights, safety, and best interests when they are most vulnerable. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: A nurse takes time to explain a new diabetic diet to a confused patient and their family. What role is this nurse performing?
explanation: Teaching patients and families how to manage their health and care for themselves at home is a core part of our educator role. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: What does professional accountability primarily require a nurse to do?

options.A: Avoid asking senior doctors for professional guidance
options.B: Cover up small mistakes to prevent hospital lawsuits
options.C: Take responsibility for their clinical actions and decisions
options.D: Work twenty-four-hour shifts without taking a break

explanation: Accountability simply means owning your choices and accepting the professional results of the care you give. We stand tall by our actions! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is following a strict code of ethics so important for a nurse?

options.A: It ensures the nurse receives the highest possible salary tier
options.B: It eliminates the need for any formal continuing education classes
options.C: It guarantees patient confidentiality, dignity, and fairness in care
options.D: It grants the nurse legal authority to perform major surgeries

explanation: Our ethical code is our compass. It guides us to treat every patient fairly, keep their secrets safe, and always respect their human dignity. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which statutory body is responsible for regulating nursing education and practice in Nigeria?

options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is the sole legal regulatory authority for the nursing profession in the country. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of regulatory bodies like the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria?

options.A: To manage the commercial business accounts of private hospitals
options.B: To protect the public by ensuring safe and competent nursing practice
options.C: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.D: To decide which political party wins national health elections

explanation: Spot on! Professional councils exist primarily to keep the public safe by setting high educational and ethical standards for all practicing nurses. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)
